goal: Let the GUI and other frontends load a UTXO snapshot through the node interface instead of touching chainstate internals directly
Add progress notifications so users see feedback during multi-minute snapshot loads instead of a frozen UI
reviewability: Stale, needs rebase after 17 force-pushes over a year, though prior review rounds are resolved
Wait for a fresh rebase before investing more review time
agreement: Strong support because it is the right way to expose snapshot loading to GUI users (pinheadmz)
Verified by testing against a real GUI branch (Sjors)
Design concerns about the interface shape were resolved through iteration with no remaining objection (ryanofsky)

categories.name: ipc
why: P2 because it builds the interface boundary needed for GUI and multiprocess separation of snapshot loading
Unblocks two downstream GUI PRs (Qt and QML) that depend on this interface
Falls short of P1 since no external consumer has actually merged against it yet

categories.name: kernel
why: P3 because it only adds one small additive notification hook to the kernel-node boundary
No external kernel consumer has requested this specific hook
Marginal relative to core kernel API completeness work the category prioritizes

categories.name: rpc
why: P3 because it collapses distinct RPC error codes into one generic internal-error code, a compatibility-sensitive change
The risk was worked through via multiple revisions rather than ignored
No external RPC consumer has complained about the error-code change

categories.name: validation
why: P4 because it only adds a UI progress hook to the existing snapshot-loading loop, not a correctness or acceptance-rule change
The one performance concern, excessive notification frequency, was fixed by batching to every 100,000 coins
